$comment: EVERY PUBLISHED SET IN THE KIT, and what this catalog does about it. Generated from the kit walk (.github/workflows/figma-refs.yml) joined to the @CatalogComponent references in the sources; CatalogKitCoverageTest holds the two together in both directions, so a set cannot be quietly dropped and an exclusion cannot outlive the limitation that earned it. A row may also carry `cells`: per sheet, WHY that sheet falls short of the set's published cells. How far short is not written here — that is a number, and kit-cells.json carries it; KitCellCoverageTest holds the reason against the count, so a reason cannot outlive its gap either. Out of scope, and not listed: the kit's own internals (names beginning '.', and the 'Base components' each page builds its published set from) and the 1072-component Icons page, which is an icon set rather than a component inventory.

Compose puts the image container painter on Button and Card; IconButton takes no painter, so there is no round image-backed button to invoke.

cells.remote-catalog: All ten are the `Alignment=Icon right` column. `RemoteCompactButton` has ONE icon slot and it leads, so a trailing icon is not something the component takes, and putting a glyph in the label to fake one would publish a picture of this catalog rather than of the library — the same absence the Wear column states for the same ten. The nine `Disabled=Yes` cells this row used to be short of are now drawn, and three of them are the disabled FILLED button to the byte, because `RemoteButtonDefaults.buttonColors` leaves the disabled pair at its defaults; they are published under `knownDuplicate` so the collapse is on the sheet instead of behind it.

Twenty are the `Outline` column, and they are unreachable rather than undrawn: `RemoteOutlinedCard` is the TITLE-LESS container, and neither `RemoteTitleCard` nor `RemoteAppCard` takes a border or a border colour at `remote-material3-1.0.0-alpha10` — there is no argument to pass. `Title Card 1, Style=Outline, Content type=Text` was the twentieth all along: `Card/Outlined` named it while drawing the title-less outlined container, which is not a picture of a title card, so the cell counted as covered by a comparison it was not making ([#149](https://github.com/yschimke/wear-m3-catalog/issues/149)). Five are `Background Image`: the same shape one parameter over, no painter on either function ([#157](https://github.com/yschimke/wear-m3-catalog/issues/157)). The image-backed BUTTON cells beside them ARE drawn, broken, because `RemoteButton` does take a painter — the difference is an API to call, not a working one. The remaining four are `Title Card 3`, whose layout puts the timestamp under the subtitle with no body at all; neither `RemoteTitleCard` nor Wear's `TitleCard` arranges that.

All four are `Size = Long | Short`, and the blocker is the kit's rather than the library's — the same one the `catalog` row states. The sweep is an argument here too (`sweepAngle` on `RemoteCurvedProgressIndicator`, which is what draws this rail at all, since `remote-material3` publishes no level indicator), so the API reaches those cells; the kit does not publish the two angles they draw. They are bound to no variable and the cells export as flattened SVGs, so the numbers live in that path data and guessing one would put an invented angle under the kit's name.

Fifty-four are `Segments=6..14`, the SEGMENTED ring: `remote-material3` publishes `RemoteCircularProgressIndicator` and `RemoteCurvedProgressIndicator` and no segmented function at all, so unlike the Wear column — where those cells belong to `SegmentedCircularProgressIndicator` and its own set — there is nothing here to call. Twenty-four are `Type=Top Gap | Bottom Gap`: `RemoteCircularProgressIndicator` takes the `startAngle`/`endAngle` pair, so the API is not the blocker — the kit is, publishing those angles in no variable and no property, only inside the flattened SVG each gap cell exports (the same wall the Wear column hits). Six are `Stroke Width=Small`: the parameter is there, but `RemoteProgressIndicatorDefaults` publishes no small or large stroke token and the Wear pair it would borrow resolves by screen breakpoint, so the number would be invented. The `Progress=Zero, Disabled=Yes` cell this row used to be short of is drawn now: it was withheld as an empty frame, and this player draws the disabled track, so it is an ordinary comparison (#178).

The two are `Type=Page-Mid`, and the reason is the kit's rather than either library's — the same one the `catalog` row states. The two cells differ in the space ABOVE the header, which is a property of where it sits in a list rather than of the header; a component sticker is cropped to what it draws, so that space is in neither picture. This sheet builds the header from `RemoteText` (there is no `RemoteListHeader`), which changes nothing about it: a content padding is what a header has, and it says nothing about what is above the header.

sets.excluded: IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT COMPARABLE — the exclusion is about the reference, not the component. `Media/PlayerScreen` (Horologist's `PlayerScreen`, see sections/MediaControls.kt) reproduces this set, but the published cell `71575:22329` does not EXPORT as the player: its `.Base / Media / Album Artwork/Primary NEW` child composites over the full 192×192, and exported on its own it stops compositing and covers everything, so the reference image is an opaque purple wash. A comparison against that reports the whole frame and means nothing, so the mapping is withdrawn rather than published. The two `AOD=Yes` cells (`71575:22344`, `71575:22375`) carry no artwork instance and export faithfully — this becomes mappable again when the exporter composites the overlay.
